docs.title: ZEN API Utilities
docs.text: Reusable, headless helpers for applications built on the generated zen_api protobuf and gRPC package.

docs.title: Contents
docs.text: The API reference includes connection and logging helpers, experiment and acquisition-plan parsing, hardware helpers, stage and sample-carrier models, workflow helpers, TCP/IP control helpers, and streaming utilities.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
Install a matching local zen_api wheel first, then install this package:

pip install zen_api-<version>-py3-none-any.whl
pip install zen_api_utils-<version>-py3-none-any.whl

OME-Zarr support is optional:

pip install "zen_api_utils[omezarr]"

docs.title: get_cameras_info_LM async
docs.text:
get_cameras_info_LM(
    cameras_service: CameraServiceStub,
) -> list[CameraInfo]

Retrieve comprehensive information about all available cameras.

Queries the ZEN API camera service to get detailed information about all cameras in the system, including their current settings, capabilities, and frame configurations. Converts ZEN API's DoubleFrame and DoubleSize objects to integer-based representations for easier handling.

Parameters:

  • cameras_service (CameraServiceStub) –

    Connected camera service stub for API calls

Returns:

  • list[CameraInfo] –

    list[CameraInfo]: List of camera information objects with converted data types

Raises:

  • Exception –

    If camera service communication fails or camera data is inaccessible

Example

channel, metadata = initialize_zenapi("config.ini") camera_service = CameraServiceStub(channel=channel, metadata=metadata) cameras = await get_cameras_list_LM(camera_service) for camera in cameras: ... print(f"Camera: {camera.name}, Size: {camera.max_frame_size.width}x{camera.max_frame_size.height}")

docs.text:
move_changers(
    channel: Channel,
    metadata: list[tuple[str, str]],
    objectives: (
        ObjectiveChangerServiceGetObjectivesResponse | None
    ) = None,
    optovars: (
        OptovarServiceGetOptovarsResponse | None
    ) = None,
    reflectors: (
        ReflectorChangerServiceGetReflectorsResponse | None
    ) = None,
    filters: (
        FilterWheelServiceGetFiltersResponse | None
    ) = None,
    objective_position: int | None = None,
    optovar_position: int | None = None,
    reflector_position: int | None = None,
    filterwheel_position: int | None = None,
) -> dict[str, Any]

Move microscope changers to specified positions based on keyword arguments. This function is robust and handles situations where not all services are available.

Parameters:

  • channel (Channel) –

    gRPC channel for communication

  • metadata (list[tuple[str, str]]) –

    gRPC metadata for authentication

  • objectives (ObjectiveChangerServiceGetObjectivesResponse | None, default: None ) –

    Available objectives data (optional, will be fetched if service available)

  • optovars (OptovarServiceGetOptovarsResponse | None, default: None ) –

    Available optovars data (optional, will be fetched if service available)

  • reflectors (ReflectorChangerServiceGetReflectorsResponse | None, default: None ) –

    Available reflectors data (optional, will be fetched if service available)

  • filters (FilterWheelServiceGetFiltersResponse | None, default: None ) –

    Available filters data (optional, will be fetched if service available)

  • objective_position (int, default: None ) –

    Target position for objective changer

  • optovar_position (int, default: None ) –

    Target position for optovar changer

  • reflector_position (int, default: None ) –

    Target position for reflector changer

  • filterwheel_position (int, default: None ) –

    Target position for filterwheel changer

Returns:

  • dict ( dict[str, Any] ) –

    Dictionary containing the results of each movement operation with current positions. Includes 'skipped' entries for unavailable services and 'warnings' for service failures.

Note
  • If a service cannot be initialized, the operation will be skipped with a warning
  • Only successfully initialized services will be used for movement operations
  • The function continues execution even if some services fail to initialize
Example

docs.title: This will attempt to move all requested changers, skipping unavailable services
docs.text: results = await move_changers( ... channel=channel, ... metadata=metadata, ... objective_position=2, ... optovar_position=1, ... reflector_position=3, ... filterwheel_position=2 ... ) print(f"Successful moves: {[k for k, v in results.items() if v and v.get('status') == 'success']}") print(f"Skipped services: {results['skipped']}")

  • objective_position (int, default: None ) –

    Target position for objective changer

  • optovar_position (int, default: None ) –

    Target position for optovar changer

  • reflector_position (int, default: None ) –

    Target position for reflector changer

  • filterwheel_position (int, default: None ) –

    Target position for filterwheel changer

Returns:

  • Only available services will be used for movement operations
  • The function continues execution even if some services are unavailable

docs.title: zen_api_utils.extract_czexp_plan
docs.text:
Extract a provisional CZI/CZMBI acquisition plan from a ZEN Experiment XML file.

Disclaimer: This script is intended for experimental use and may not cover all edge cases of ZEN Experiment XML files.

Run from the repository root:

python experimental\extract_czexp_plan.py experimental\ZEN_API_Test_CD7_split.czexp

Write a reduced JSON plan and a CZMBI file in one call:

python experimental\extract_czexp_plan.py `
    experimental\ZEN_API_Test_CD7_split.czexp `
    --reduced `
    --output experimental\plan.json `
    --czmbi-output experimental\hcs.czmbi

The JSON plan is always written first. When --czmbi-output is present, the script reloads that JSON and projects its first acquisition block to CZMBI 1.0. CZMBI generation requires split-scene acquisition with one planned CZI per scene. When ZEN does not expose exact output names, the generated CZMBI uses deterministic suggested_filename values that must be validated against actual ZEN output.

Reads axis names (T, C, Z, Y, X) and per-axis scales from the OME-ZARR 0.5 metadata stored in zarr.json and wraps the highest-resolution array as a dask-backed xr.DataArray with physically-spaced coordinates so that ndv shows correct proportions (including Z depth) and labelled sliders.
